rows.answer: Assuming "best" means on-time delivery rate on Delivered loads, among the 40 carriers with at least 30 delivered loads: Pioneer Carriers 98 LLC leads at 92.94% on time across 170 loads, with a 14.71% margin. Big River Hauling Co. (92.82%) and Eagle Transit 97 LLC (92.66%) follow closely. Midsouth Freight LLC has the best margin in the top group (14.79%) and is third-tier on on-time at 92.18%. Two of the top 15 carry a Conditional safety rating (Lone Star Lines 84 LLC and Blue Ridge Lines 11 LLC), and Big River is Unrated, so check those before assigning them high-value freight.
sql:
WITH d AS (
  SELECT l.carrier_id,
         COUNT(*) AS delivered,
         SUM(CASE WHEN l.delivery_actual <= l.delivery_appt THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS on_time,
         ROUND(AVG(l.shipper_rate - l.carrier_cost), 2) AS avg_margin,
         ROUND(100.0 * SUM(l.shipper_rate - l.carrier_cost) / NULLIF(SUM(l.shipper_rate), 0), 2) AS margin_pct
  FROM loads l
  WHERE l.status = 'Delivered' AND l.carrier_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY l.carrier_id
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= 30
)
SELECT c.name AS carrier, c.safety_rating, d.delivered,
       ROUND(100.0 * d.on_time / d.delivered, 2) AS on_time_pct,
       d.avg_margin, d.margin_pct
FROM d JOIN carriers c ON c.carrier_id = d.carrier_id
ORDER BY on_time_pct DESC, d.delivered DESC
LIMIT 15

SELECT COUNT(*) AS carriers_with_30plus_delivered FROM (
  SELECT carrier_id FROM loads WHERE status='Delivered' AND carrier_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY carrier_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 30
)
LIMIT 200

rows.answer: Margin is holding around 14.5% through August, then slipped to 13.81% in September, the lowest month in the data. September's margin per load also fell to $246.13, from $262.25 in August. Delivered volume dipped too, to 2,222 loads from roughly 2,320 a month. I used pickup month for the grouping, so September's figures may shift a little if loads picked up late in August have not yet been delivered.
sql:
SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', pickup_appt) AS month,
       COUNT(*) AS delivered_loads,
       ROUND(SUM(shipper_rate), 2) AS total_rate,
       ROUND(SUM(carrier_cost), 2) AS total_cost,
       ROUND(SUM(shipper_rate - carrier_cost), 2) AS total_margin,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(shipper_rate - carrier_cost) / SUM(shipper_rate), 2) AS margin_pct,
       ROUND(AVG(shipper_rate - carrier_cost), 2) AS avg_margin_per_load
FROM loads
WHERE status = 'Delivered'
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month
LIMIT 200

Assuming September is based on the accessorial's created_at date, the only delivery facility with linked detention charges in September 2026 is Harbor Foods DC - Atlanta (GA), with 10 charges totaling $2,343.75. That answer is incomplete, though: 230 of the 240 September detention charges ($50,475.00 of $52,818.75) have no delivery facility on the load, so they can't be attributed to a facility. Treat Harbor Foods DC - Atlanta as the only confirmed result, not the overall leader.
sql:
SELECT f.facility_id, f.name, f.city, f.state,
       COUNT(a.accessorial_id) AS detention_count,
       ROUND(SUM(a.amount), 2) AS detention_total
FROM accessorials a
JOIN loads l ON l.load_id = a.load_id
JOIN facilities f ON f.facility_id = l.delivery_facility_id

  AND strftime('%Y-%m', a.created_at) = '2026-09'
GROUP BY f.facility_id, f.name, f.city, f.state
ORDER BY detention_total DESC
LIMIT 10

Bluegrass Haulers LLC had the most late deliveries on September 2026 pickups: 17 of its 26 delivered loads (65.38%) arrived after the appointment. The next highest was Delta Express 91 LLC and Silver Spur Freight 78 LLC, with 6 late each. I counted September by actual pickup date and used Delivered loads only.

sql:
WITH sept AS (
  SELECT l.carrier_id, l.delivery_actual, l.delivery_appt
  FROM loads l
  WHERE l.status = 'Delivered'
    AND strftime('%Y-%m', l.pickup_actual) = '2026-09'
),
agg AS (
  SELECT carrier_id,
         COUNT(*) AS delivered,
         SUM(CASE WHEN delivery_actual > delivery_appt THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS late
  FROM sept
  GROUP BY carrier_id
)
SELECT c.name AS carrier, a.delivered, a.late,
       ROUND(100.0 * a.late / a.delivered, 2) AS late_pct
FROM agg a
JOIN carriers c ON c.carrier_id = a.carrier_id
ORDER BY a.late DESC, late_pct DESC
LIMIT 5

Bluegrass Haulers LLC (carrier 42) has the worst on-time delivery rate among carriers with at least 50 delivered loads: 75 of 162 delivered loads arrived on time, or 46.3%, with 53.7% late. That is far behind the next-worst carrier, Redline Carriers 62 LLC, at 83.89%. This covers all delivered loads in the data (April through September 2026), and a delivery counts as on time when delivery_actual is at or before delivery_appt.
sql:
WITH d AS (
  SELECT c.carrier_id, c.name,
         COUNT(*) AS delivered_loads,
         SUM(CASE WHEN l.delivery_actual <= l.delivery_appt THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS on_time_loads
  FROM loads l
  JOIN carriers c ON c.carrier_id = l.carrier_id
  WHERE l.status = 'Delivered'
    AND l.delivery_actual IS NOT NULL AND l.delivery_appt IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY c.carrier_id, c.name
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= 50
)
SELECT carrier_id, name, delivered_loads, on_time_loads,
       ROUND(100.0 * on_time_loads / delivered_loads, 2) AS on_time_pct,
       ROUND(100.0 * (delivered_loads - on_time_loads) / delivered_loads, 2) AS late_pct
FROM d
ORDER BY on_time_pct ASC, delivered_loads DESC
LIMIT 10
